1.title: Switch off the breaker power.
1.say: Find the breaker labeled for your room. Flip its little handle to off.
placements: breaker handle for your entry and bedroom lights → OFF position in the open gray breaker box (in the video: middle row labeled ENTRY BEDROOM 1 2)
watch_for: if the wall light still turns on, you flipped the wrong breaker
if the handle sits in the middle, push it fully to off
1.check_yourself: It should look like the little handle points to off.
1.safety: Test the wall light so you know the power is dead.

2.title: Take off the switch cover.
2.say: Unscrew the four little cover screws. Lift the cover straight off the wall.
placements: four little cover screws → out of the white double cover with a drill (in the video: top and bottom holes beside the door lock)
white double cover → off the wall to show two white switches (in the video: left side of the white door frame)
watch_for: if the cover will not lift, a screw is still holding it
if the paint peels, you pried too hard against the wall
2.check_yourself: It should look like two white switches with no cover.
2.safety: Do not poke tools into the open switch gaps.

3.title: Pull out the old switch.
3.say: Loosen the top and bottom switch screws. Ease the right switch out of the hole. Cut its two back wires to free it.
placements: right white switch → out of the right side of the blue wall hole into your hand (in the video: right spot beside the door frame)
two dark back wires of the old switch → cut free with cutters leaving short ends hanging from the wall hole (in the video: loose wires from right hole)
bare ground wire → unscrewed from the little green screw on the old switch (in the video: side of the removed switch)
watch_for: if you pull the left switch, you grabbed the wrong side that stays
if bare ends touch, the breaker can trip when power returns
3.check_yourself: It should look like one switch left with loose wires beside it.
3.safety: Keep the bare wire ends apart so they cannot touch.

4.title: Join the ground wires safely.
4.say: Twist the green new switch wire to the bare wall wire. Screw a yellow cap on tight.
placements: green wire from the new white switch → twisted with the bare copper wire from the wall box and closed with a yellow twist cap (in the video: hanging below the right wall hole)
watch_for: if the yellow cap falls off, the wires were not twisted together first
if shiny copper shows outside the cap, push the wires deeper
4.check_yourself: It should look like a yellow cap holding green and bare wires.
4.safety: Touch no bare copper while the breaker is off.

5.title: Join white wires and cap blue wire.
5.say: Twist the white new switch wire with the white wall bundle. Twist the red cap back on tight. Push a yellow cap on the lone blue switch wire.
placements: white wire from the new smart switch → twisted into the bundle of three white wall wires in the back of the blue box and closed with a red twist cap (in the video: middle of right hole)
blue wire from the new smart switch → closed alone with a yellow twist cap and left unused (in the video: hanging near the door lock side)
watch_for: if white ends pull out, the red cap is loose and needs another twist
if the blue end shows copper, it needs a yellow cap alone
5.check_yourself: It should look like capped white bundle and capped blue wire.
5.safety: Keep the blue end fully covered so it cannot short.

6.title: Join black and red power wires.
6.say: Strip the two black wall ends about half an inch. Cap the black switch wire to one black wall wire. Cap the red switch wire to the other black wall wire.
placements: black wire from the new smart switch → twisted to one black wall wire and closed with a yellow twist cap (in the video: lower right near the wall hole)
red wire from the new smart switch → twisted to the other black wall wire and closed with a yellow twist cap (in the video: middle right near the wall hole)
watch_for: if the light stays dead later, a yellow cap is loose on black
if copper shows outside a cap, untwist and tuck it fully inside
6.check_yourself: It should look like two yellow caps on black pairs near the hole.
6.safety: Keep the two capped pairs apart while you work.

7.title: Push in and screw new switch.
7.say: Fold the wires gently back into the hole. Set the new switch beside the old one. Drive the top and bottom screws snug.
placements: new white smart switch with connected wires → pushed into the right side of the blue wall box beside the left old switch and fixed with top and bottom mounting screws using a drill (in the video: right hole next to the white door frame)
watch_for: if the switch will not go in, wires are bunched behind it
if it feels crooked, the top and bottom tabs are not flat to the wall
7.check_yourself: It should look like two white switches side by side uncovered.
7.safety: Keep fingers clear of the drill tip while driving screws.

8.title: Put the cover back on.
8.say: Hold the double cover over both switches. Drive its four little screws snug.
placements: white double cover → over both white switches on the wall beside the door lock (in the video: left of the smart door lock)
four little cover screws → into the cover corners with a small driver (in the video: top and bottom holes around the switches)
watch_for: if the cover rocks, one corner screw is tighter than the others
if the green light is hidden, the cover is upside down
8.check_yourself: It should look like a clean white cover with a green light.
